title: Why do stores put essentials at the back?
sources: Food Marketing Institute Supermarket Layout Studies
Cornell University Food and Brand Lab

lines.text: Why is the gallon of milk or loaf of bread always placed at the furthest back corner of the grocery store?
lines.caps: Why is the *milk | always hidden in the very *back?

lines.text: It is not an accident; it is a calculated psychological trap designed by retail architects.
lines.caps: A calculated *retail trap | designed to make you *spend!

lines.text: Milk and eggs are the most frequently purchased staples in American households.
lines.caps: Staples like milk and *eggs | are bought *most often

lines.text: To grab that one carton of milk, you are forced to walk past dozens of brightly packaged impulse items.
lines.caps: Forces you to *walk past | hundreds of impulse *snacks

lines.text: Endcaps, bakery aromas, and eye-level snack displays lure you into tossing items into your cart.
lines.caps: Fresh bakery *aromas | and displays lure your *cravings

lines.text: Retail studies show over sixty percent of items in a typical grocery cart were completely unplanned purchases.
To save money, write a strict grocery list and stick to it without looking at the side displays.
lines.caps: Stick strictly to your *list | to beat supermarket *tricks!
